name: Event
description: An upcoming or past Harvard in Tech event. Stored as a markdown file in the `events` content collection; rendered in the landing page's Upcoming Events section.

name: TeamMember
description: A Board of Directors / team member. Stored as a markdown file in the `team` content collection; rendered in the landing page's Board of Directors section.

name: Page
description: A free-form site page (About, chapter pages, etc.) in the `pages` content collection. Body markdown is the page content. Per-page SEO overrides (`metaTitle`, `metaDescription`, `ogImage`) and an optional embed (`embedUrl`/`embedHtml`) mirror the blog collection (CMS-ready for when a pages route renders these entries).

name: BlogPost
description: A news/blog post in the `blog` content collection. Per-page SEO overrides (`metaTitle`, `metaDescription`, `ogImage`) and an optional embed (`embedUrl`/`embedHtml`) are all optional.

name: Settings
description: Site-wide editable settings singleton (`src/data/settings.json`): title, description, contact email, footer, socials, plus integrations/discoverability (Google Analytics id, Givebutter account id, custom head/body HTML). Loaded by every layout; edited by the CMS as a file collection.

name: Nav
description: Editable navigation menu singleton (`src/data/nav.json`) with nested dropdowns, edited from /admin → Settings. Loaded by the base layout, which injects a Chapters group derived from the chapters collection — so the Chapters menu is not stored here.

name: Chapter
description: A regional Harvard in Tech chapter (Boston & Cambridge, DC and DMV Area, London, New York City, Seattle / Pacific Northwest, SF & Bay Area). Stored as a markdown file in the `chapters` content collection; rendered on per-chapter routes at /chapters/<slug>, and the source the base layout derives the nav Chapters dropdown from. Optional fields (`leads`, `links`) prove a chapter with no leads listed still renders. `order` is an optional PIN, not a required rank: entries that carry no `order` sort alphabetically by city, which is how the roster orders itself so a new chapter needs no renumbering. See Community for the interest-based counterpart.

name: VolunteerProject
description: An open volunteer project shown in the grid on /volunteer. Stored as a markdown file in the `projects` content collection and edited in the CMS, so organizers can open and close projects without a code change. `image` is the project thumbnail; `applyUrl` is where an interested volunteer goes. `active: false` retires a project without deleting its record. `startDate` / `endDate` are DISPLAY-ONLY — they format into a range on the card and detail header but never gate visibility, because on a static build a date-expired project would linger until the next deploy and then vanish without anyone touching the CMS; `active` alone decides what appears.

name: Testimonial
description: A member quote shown in the testimonials band on the /donate Momentum Fund campaign page. Stored in the `testimonials` content collection. Production starts with none — the band hides itself entirely when the collection is empty, so the page reads as finished before any quotes are collected.

name: VolunteerPageCopy
description: Editable copy for /volunteer: headline, intro, the four "Why Volunteer" benefit blocks, and the projects-section framing including the empty-state message. Now a single-entry markdown collection (`volunteerPage`) so it renders as a real screen in /admin — it used to be `src/data/volunteerPage.json`, read through the same readSingleton path as settings/nav, which the CMS models no editor for. That file survives as the FALLBACK: the collection entry wins when present, and deleting it leaves the page rendering the committed copy rather than a blank hero, because the editor has no notion of a required singleton and lets the last entry go.

name: DonatePageCopy
description: The page s FRAME fields — hero headline named/generic, subhead, photo, and the closing ask — now live on the `donate` PageCopy entry so an editor can rewrite them; `donatePage.json` is the fallback. `accomplishments`, `pillars`, and `donateUrl` already migrated to their own collections in the launch-ready-editing cycle. What remains below describes the singleton s full shape, which is still what the route grafts its content-sourced values onto. Editable copy for the /donate Momentum Fund campaign page, held in the `donatePage.json` singleton under the data root. `accomplishments` is the campaign's track record — the concrete things the community has already done (community size, reach, events, new chapters) — shown between the stats band and the story, because the campaign doc asks a reader to fund momentum that is already visible rather than a promise. `stats` are the headline figures the story title ("And Every Number Represents a Story") refers back to. `donateUrl` stays empty until a donation platform is chosen, at which point the CTA stops falling back to a giving-inquiry mailto. `donorTiers` are the giving levels the Donor Recognition wall groups by; each carries the `id` a Donor's `tier` matches on, mirroring `levels` in `sponsorPage.json`, and renaming a tier is a copy edit while its `id` stays the stable key.

name: MediaAsset
description: One image in the media library. Records live in the `{ assets: [] }` manifest singleton at `src/data/media.json` (the package's MEDIA_MANIFEST_PATH), which the CMS media library writes. Disk decides which assets exist — the `public/images` scan — while this record decides what is KNOWN about one, above all its alt text. `filename` is the identity: a path WITHIN `public/images`, so it may contain `/` for a nested asset (`gallery/event-05.jpg`). An explicit empty `alt` is a deliberate "this image is decorative", not a missing value.

name: Community
description: A non-geographic Harvard in Tech community (Founders, AI) — the interest-based counterpart to a Chapter. Stored as a markdown file in the `communities` content collection; rendered on per-community routes at /communities/<slug>, and the source the base layout derives the nav Communities entries from (alongside the hand-authored WhatsApp link in nav.json). Shares the Chapter shape so both render through the same page components; `name` replaces `city` because a community has no location. Events join a community through the same `chapter` tag they use for chapters, so editors learn no second field.

name: Sponsor
description: One organization supporting Harvard Alumni in Tech, shown on the /sponsor wall. Stored as a markdown file in the `sponsors` content collection. `tier` groups the wall by partnership level and must match a level id in `sponsorPage.json` — an unmatched tier is reported rather than silently dropping the sponsor. `placeholder: true` marks an ILLUSTRATIVE entry: the wall then renders an explicit 'example, not actual sponsors' notice, so a page seeded with sample logos can never be mistaken for a live sponsor list. Real sponsors omit the flag. The collection starts empty in production, where the wall renders nothing at all.

name: SponsorPageCopy
description: Now a single-entry markdown collection (`sponsorPage`) with `src/data/sponsorPage.json` as the fallback, so the pitch is editable in /admin instead of being a code change. Its `levels` array moved out to the separate SponsorLevel collection — a benefits list inside a list of levels is not expressible in the editor. Editable copy for /sponsor, held in the `sponsorPage.json` singleton under the data root — the same model as VolunteerPageCopy and DonatePageCopy, so the pitch, the partnership levels, and the legal line are all CMS edits rather than code changes. `levels` are the partnership tiers a sponsor chooses between; each carries the `id` a Sponsor's `tier` matches on. `disclaimer` carries the Harvard Alumni Association requirement that a shared-interest group state contributions go to the group and not to Harvard University, so it is copy the team can revise without a deploy.

name: MomentumSection
description: One reorderable section in the middle of the /donate Momentum Fund campaign page, stored as a markdown file in the `momentumSections` content collection and editable from the CMS. `kind` selects the renderer: `narrative` uses the entry's own title/body/image, `goal-meter` renders a live Givebutter fundraising meter from its own `widgetId`, while `accomplishments`, `pillars`, `testimonials`, and `stats` are slots whose card data still comes from `donatePage.json`. `group` names which set of cards a slot band shows: a band with no group shows the cards with no group (the page as it renders today), so two `pillars` sections can be split into distinct bands by giving each its own group. `title` names the band both on the page and in the CMS list, falling back to the shared heading from `donatePage.json` when blank. `order` is how an editor moves a section up or down (lower appears higher); `draft` hides one without deleting it. The hero and closing CTA are a fixed frame and are not sections.

name: Donor
description: One person or household who gave to the Momentum Fund, listed on the /donate recognition wall. Stored as a markdown file in the `donors` content collection and added from the CMS. `tier` groups the wall by giving level and must match a tier id in `donatePage.json` — an unmatched or untagged donor collects in a trailing group rather than vanishing, the same tolerance the sponsor wall has. `founding` is a badge, not a tier: it renders the Founding Donor mark on whichever giving level the donor sits in. `anonymous` renders 'Anonymous donor' on the site while the entry keeps the real name for the team's records, and suppresses the outbound `url` link so an anonymous donor cannot be identified through it. `note` is the short line revealed on the card; the body is an optional longer thank-you. `draft` holds an entry back until the gift clears. The collection starts empty in production, where the wall renders its invitation state.

name: HomeSection
description: One band of the homepage, stored as a markdown file in the `homeSections` content collection and editable from the CMS — the homepage counterpart to MomentumSection. `kind` selects which component renders (`hero`, `stats`, `events`, `chapters`, `focus`, `content-hub`, `board`, `get-involved`, `giving`, `whatsapp`, `support`, `gallery`, `contact`) and an unknown value drops that one band with a warning rather than failing the build. `order` moves a band up or down (lower appears higher). Visibility is two toggles rather than one typed value, because the CMS has no select control: `comingSoon` renders the placeholder band, and `draft` removes the band and its nav item together.

name: HeroSlide
description: One slide of the homepage hero carousel, stored in the `heroSlides` content collection. Migrated out of HeroCarousel.astro's hardcoded prop defaults, which were the live content because index.astro rendered the carousel with no props. `ctas` holds up to two button links per slide. An empty collection falls back to the component's built-in defaults, so the hero is never blank.

name: HomeStat
description: One figure in the homepage stat strip under the hero, stored in the `stats` content collection. Migrated out of `homeStats` on settings.json, which held real values but had no input in the CMS — the package renders only five scalar settings fields and round-trips everything else untouched. `draft` hides one figure without disturbing the others.

name: Accomplishment
description: One card in the Momentum Fund's 'What we've accomplished so far' band, stored in the `accomplishments` content collection. Migrated out of donatePage.json, which the CMS does not model at all. The `momentumSections` entry of kind `accomplishments` still positions the band; these entries are now its content. `group` assigns the card to a band: cards with no group belong to the ungrouped band, and a card naming a group appears only in the section that names the same group.

name: Pillar
description: One card in the Momentum Fund's 'What Your Gift Powers' band, stored in the `pillars` content collection. Migrated out of donatePage.json. `icon` names one of the three inline SVG glyphs (people, book, globe) as free text validated in a lib — the same treatment `kind` and `layout` get — so an unrecognized value falls back rather than failing the build. `linkLabel`/`linkUrl` are optional; a card without them renders as plain copy. `group` assigns the card to a band: cards with no group belong to the ungrouped band, and a card naming a group appears only in the section that names the same group.

name: SponsorLevel
description: One partnership level on /sponsor, as a markdown entry in the `sponsorLevels` content collection. Migrated out of the `levels` array inside `sponsorPage.json`, which the CMS could not render an input for: a level carries a `benefits` string list INSIDE a list of levels, and the editor supports a repeatable list of scalars at top level only. One entry per level makes `benefits` a top-level list and matches the shape `pillars` and `accomplishments` already use. The ENTRY FILENAME is the stable key a Sponsor s `tier` matches on — there is deliberately no `id` frontmatter field. Two reasons point the same way: an editable id text box silently re-homes every sponsor filed under the level when retyped, and the codeyam seed adapter strips `id` (like `slug`) as a filename key, which made the collection literally unseedable while the field existed — every scenario s levels failed validation and fell back to the committed JSON with nothing visibly wrong. `chapters` and `communities` key off the filename the same way. Ordering is the site-wide `order` pin so the wall reads top-down from the biggest commitment.

name: SiteIntegrations
description: The site-wide integration keys — GA4 measurement id, the Givebutter account id, and the raw custom `<head>` / `<body>` HTML escape hatches — as a single-entry markdown collection. These have always been real editable data on the `settings.json` singleton, but the CMS settings screen renders inputs for five scalar keys plus socials and round-trips the rest untouched, so they were data with nowhere to edit them. Deliberately its own collection rather than extra fields on `pageCopy`: the editor renders every declared field for every entry, so sharing would put an analytics box on the Momentum Fund page s screen. `settings.json` remains the fallback, so deleting this entry cannot silently unhook analytics from every page. `givebutterAccountId` is the `acct=` value from Givebutter's embed snippet; blank means the widgets loader script is not shipped at all, so a site with no Givebutter account emits zero third-party markup.

name: PageCopy
description: Per-page settings an editor changes from /admin, one markdown entry per page in the `pageCopy` collection. Today it holds the single `donate` entry: the Momentum Fund page s donation-platform URL (blank keeps every giving button on the giving-inquiry mailto) plus the page s FIXED FRAME — the hero headline in its named and generic forms, the hero subhead and photo, and the closing ask s title, body, and button label. The frame is deliberately not part of the reorderable `momentumSections` middle: a page whose hero could be dragged to the bottom is a page an editor can break. Making its copy editable does not make it draggable. `donatePage.json` remains the fallback for every field.

name: CutoverProgress
description: Shared progress on the domain cutover, as the singleton `src/data/cutoverProgress.json`. One record per runbook step (S1–S9) and per open decision (D1–D5), each carrying whether it is done/answered plus the GitHub login that set it and when. Ships with everything open, which is the true state of the migration — nothing has been performed. Written from the runbook page itself via the CMS's GitHub commit path (an editor's own token, committed to the `staging` branch named in `src/data/cms.json`), so a tick is attributed to a real GitHub identity and every reader loads the same state rather than a browser-local copy. Read through `src/lib/cutoverProgress.ts`, which uses `readSingleton` so the codeyam sandbox redirect is honored and each scenario can seed a different state.
